mentions.name: Data science playground
mentions.description: A gamified data science playground for training colleagues to use Claude to write data analysis tools. It generates synthetic data resembling on-the-job datasets with statistical trends embedded in it, encrypts the answers, and puts an LLM in front of the answer file that gives warm/cold feedback as users submit their analysis results, aiming to speed up the path to data-driven results.
mentions.problem: Colleagues aren't yet comfortable using Claude to write data analysis tools, and the author wants to level them up and make getting data-driven results easier and faster.
mentions.audience: Coworkers at the author's workplace being trained to use Claude for data analysis
mentions.source_excerpt: trying my hand at vibe-coding a "data science playground" to try and level-up a couple of people into feeling comfortable using Claude to write data analysis tools. I generated a bunch of synthetic data, that looks like stuff we might encounter on the job, and embedded trends into the data that can be revealed through statistical analysis. I encrypted the answers and put a lil LLM in front of the answer file. You submit answers to the LLM and it tells you warm/cold by looking at the answer file.
